Only in Lashes for fornication, four witnesses and the mutual cursing oath: The fornicating woman and man each receive a hundred lashes, witnessed by a party of believers; A fornicator may marry only a fornicator or an idolater; such marriage is forbidden to believers; A husband accusing his wife without witnesses swears four times by God and a fifth time invokes God's curse on himself if lying; she averts punishment by four counter-oaths and a fifth invoking God's wrath; Whether the husband who accuses his wife bears any liability [contrast between the texts]; Wife suspected of adultery drinks 'water of bitterness' as an ordeal; Whoever accuses a chaste woman without four witnesses is flogged eighty lashes and his testimony is never accepted; Who is barred from marrying an unchaste woman [divergence between the texts]; Judges told to let no pity hold them back from carrying out a fixed punishment; How many lashes a flogging may have [contrast between the texts]; A man accused swears a curse-oath before the altar, and God judges guilty and innocent; Who swears, and how, when a husband suspects his wife of adultery without witnesses [divergence between the texts]; Adultery done in secret with no witness and not caught in the act; and 4 more.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God speaks to the prophet face to face, as a man speaks to his friend (weight 6.0). Pair score 6.0.

Only in Death and burial of Moses: Moses dies 'by the mouth of YHWH' (al pi YHWH); At death his eye was not dim nor his vigor abated; God (he) buries the prophet; no one knows his grave to this day; Successor filled with spirit of wisdom through laying on of hands; No prophet arose again like Moses whom God knew face to face; From Nebo/Pisgah God shows Moses the whole land from Gilead to Dan to the western sea; Moses is 120 years old; Thirty days of mourning for a leader; Leader shown the whole land from a mountaintop but may not enter.

Only in The chain of revelation; Jesus, word and spirit; 'say not three': The angels brought near (al-muqarrabūn) to God; God spoke to Moses directly (kallama taklīman); Jesus is God's word cast to Mary and a spirit from him; Catalogue of prophets who received revelation, from Noah to Jesus; People of the Book, do not go to excess (lā taghlū) in your religion; The Messiah does not disdain to be a servant of God, nor do the angels brought near; Do not say 'three'; God is only one god (rejection of a triad); First servant song: God's chosen servant with his spirit brings justice to the nations without crying out; a bruised reed he will not break; Of the messengers before you, some we have related to you and some we have not; God gave David the Psalms (Zabur); Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [contrast between the texts]; Denial that God has taken a son (walad); and 2 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): echo. kabbēḏ ʾeṯ ʾāḇîḵā wə-ʾeṯ ʾimmeḵā kaʾăšer ṣiwwəḵā YHWH ... ləmaʿan yîṭaḇ lāḵ vs. wa-waṣṣaynā l-insāna bi-wālidayhi iḥsānan. Deuteronomy's 'as YHWH commanded you' (ṣiwwəḵā) matches the Quran's 'we enjoined' (waṣṣaynā), both from the root ṣ-w-y.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life (weight 5.3). Pair score 5.3.

[response between the texts]; Sabbath grounded in the memory of slavery in Egypt; Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts]; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); and 10 more.

Only in Kindness to parents, thirty months of bearing and weaning, the prayer at forty and the son who says 'Uff': God enjoins humans to be good to their parents; On reaching full strength at forty, a man prays to be grateful for favor on himself and his parents and for righteous offspring; A son says 'Uff!' to his parents who plead with him, scorning resurrection as 'tales of the ancients'; His mother bore him with hardship and delivered him with hardship; bearing and weaning take thirty months; The damned are told: you used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them; today you are repaid with humiliation; The mother's pain in bearing children: penalty, or ground of gratitude [divergence between the texts]; For all there are degrees (darajat) according to what they did; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; A son who rejects his parents: the charge and the penalty [divergence between the texts]; Stubborn and rebellious son, glutton and drunkard, stoned by the men of his city; Whoever does good does it for his own soul; whoever does evil, it is against it; Unbelievers dismiss the revelation as 'tales of the ancients' (asatir al-awwalin) they could equal.

title: The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb ↔ The recited commandments (the Quranic decalogue)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Deut: kabbēd ʾet-ʾāvîkhā wə-ʾet-ʾimmekhā ... ləmaʿan yaʾărîkhūn yāmêkhā û-ləmaʿan yîṭav lākh ʿal-hā-ʾădāmāh. Q: wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan. 'Honour' becomes 'kindness', and the promise of long life in the land is dropped. Deut: lōʾ tirṣāḥ; wə-lōʾ tinʾāf; wə-lōʾ-taʿăneh və-rēʿăkhā ʿēd šāwʾ, absolute. Q qualifies and widens: wa-lā taqtulū l-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi (with an exception); wa-lā taqrabū l-fawāḥisha mā ẓahara minhā wa-mā baṭana (all indecency, not only adultery); wa-idhā qultum fa-ʿdilū wa-law kāna dhā qurbā (just speech even against kin). Theft is absent. Deut, right after the Decalogue: lōʾ tāsurû yāmîn û-śəmōʾl bə-khol-ha-dderekh ... tēlēkhû. Q, right after its list: wa-anna hādhā ṣirāṭī mustaqīman fa-ttabiʿūhu wa-lā tattabiʿū l-subula fa-tafarraqa bikum. The single road versus side paths, placed at the same point.

title: Superscription, 'vapor of vapors' and the endless cycles of nature ↔ Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: the sun runs to its resting place (mustaqarr).

passages.note: The sun runs to its resting place (mustaqarr) (wə-zāraḥ ha-ššemeš û-ḇāʾ ha-ššāmeš wə-ʾel-məqômô šôʾēp̄ zôrēaḥ hûʾ šām vs. wa-sh-shamsu tajrī li-mustaqarrin lahā dhālika taqdīru l-ʿazīzi l-ʿalīm. Only in Superscription, 'vapor of vapors' and the endless cycles of nature: Endless cycles: the sun rises and pants back to its place, the wind circles, rivers run to the sea which is never full; All things are wearisome; the eye is not sated with seeing nor the ear filled with hearing; A generation goes and a generation comes, but the earth stands forever; There is no remembrance of former people nor will there be of those yet to come; What has been is what will be; there is nothing new under the sun; The speaker Qohelet ('the assembler') is presented as son of David and king over Israel in Jerusalem (royal fiction); What profit (yitron) has a man from all his toil under the sun?; 'Hevel havalim': vapor of vapors, all is vapor (vanity, futility, transience).

Only in Signs of the dead earth, night, sun, moon and the laden ship: The night is a sign: God strips (naslakh) the day from it and they are in darkness; A sign: God carried their offspring in the laden ship, and made for them similar things to ride; God measured stations (manazil) for the moon until it returns like an old dried palm-stalk; Asked to spend, unbelievers retort 'shall we feed one whom God could feed if he willed?'; God made the flood ship (or its survivors) a sign for all the worlds; The hero is saved with those with him in the laden ark (al-fulk al-mashḥūn); The sun comes forth like a bridegroom from his chamber and rejoices like a strong man to run his course; God made the sun a radiance and the moon a light with measured stations, to count years and reckoning; Sun and moon each swim in an orbit (falak); God created humans (and things) in pairs, male and female; Scoffers ask the prophet to hasten the punishment; it is held back only by an appointed term and will come suddenly; Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons; and 1 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. ka-ʿăṣāmîm bə-ḇeṭen ha-mməlēʾâ kāḵâ lōʾ ṯēḏaʿ ʾeṯ-maʿăśēh hā-ʾĕlōhîm vs. wa-yaʿlamu mā fī l-arḥām: what grows in the womb is hidden from humans and known to God. Qohelet joins it to the way of the wind (ha-rûaḥ), the Quran to the Hour and the rain.
Shared motifs, rarest first: God alone knows the Hour, sends rain, knows what is in wombs; no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow or in what land it will die (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Cast your bread upon the waters; rejoice in youth: As you do not know the way of the wind (or spirit), or how bones grow in the womb of the pregnant, so you do not know the work of God; Send out your bread on the face of the waters, for after many days you will find it; Give a portion to seven or even to eight, for you do not know what disaster may come; Light is sweet and it is pleasant for the eyes to see the sun; Rejoice, young man, in your youth and walk in the ways of your heart, but know that for all these God will bring you into judgment; In the morning sow your seed and in the evening do not withhold your hand, for you do not know which will prosper; If clouds are full they empty rain; where the tree falls, north or south, there it lies; He who watches the wind will not sow, and he who regards the clouds will not reap; Youth and the dawn of life (shaharut, 'blackness of hair') are vapor; Graded numerical saying: 'Three things... and four...' (x / x+1).

Only in God's signs, the inexhaustible words, and the five things only God knows: Creating and resurrecting all of you is for God like a single soul; Waves overwhelm the ship like canopies (zulal); If all trees were pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas, were ink, God's words would not be exhausted; The religion of the fathers invoked, held to or renounced [contrast between the texts]; Whoever rejects false gods (taghut) and believes in God grasps the firmest handhold that never breaks; On the Day no parent can avail his child, nor child his parent; Only God knows when the mountain goats and hinds give birth and counts their months; Seafarers cry to God in a storm; what they do once rescued [divergence between the texts]; Sailors in a storm call on God sincerely, vow thanks, and transgress once saved; Rejecters reply 'we follow what we found our fathers upon'; Sun and moon are subjected, each running to an appointed term; God makes the night pass into the day and the day into the night; and 1 more.

passages.note: Whether death is the end: asked, held by sceptics, or answered by resurrection [response between the texts] (The sceptic's view of death, voiced in the HB and refuted in the Quran. Qohelet: miqreh ʾeḥāḏ lāhem kə-môṯ zeh kēn môṯ zeh ... hak-kōl šāḇ ʾel he-ʿāp̄ār; mî yôḏēaʿ rûaḥ bənê hā-ʾāḏām hā-ʿōlâ hîʾ lə-māʿlâ. (mî yôḏēaʿ) the Quran replies that they have no knowledge (ʿilm), only conjecture, and 45:26 affirms the gathering to the Day of Resurrection. passages.note: 'Hevel havalim': vapor of vapors, all is vapor (vanity, futility, transience) (worldly life as play; the hereafter is 'the true life' (al-hayawan))
passages.text: وَمَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَآ إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ لَهِىَ ٱلْحَيَوَانُ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Both call this life empty: wa-mā hādhihi l-ḥayātu d-dunyā illā lahwun wa-laʿib vs. mispar yəmê ḥayyê heḇlô wə-yaʿăśēm ka-ṣṣēl. Qohelet ends agnostic, mî yaggîd lā-ʾāḏām mah-yihyeh ʾaḥărâw (who will tell man what comes after him; cf. Eccl 9:5, 9:10, no reckoning in Sheol). The Quran answers: inna d-dāra l-ākhirata la-hiya l-ḥayawān, the next abode is the real life.

Shared motifs, rarest first: This life is fleeting; whether anything real follows it [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); 'Hevel havalim': vapor of vapors, all is vapor (vanity, futility, transience) (weight 5.3). Pair score 12.0.

Only in Wealth unenjoyed, the stillborn better off, desire unfilled: Whatever has come to be has already been named; man cannot dispute with one stronger than he; All man's toil is for his mouth, yet the appetite (nefesh) is never filled; Better the sight of the eyes than the wandering of desire; A man with a hundred children and long life who is unsatisfied and has no burial: the stillborn (nefel) is better off than he; Even if he lived a thousand years twice and saw no good, do not all go to one place?; God gives a man riches, possessions and honor but not the power to enjoy them; a stranger enjoys them; Who will bring him to see what will be after him?; Sufferer wishes he had died in the womb or been a hidden stillborn; Human days on earth are a shadow.

Only in God's earth is wide; every soul tastes death; signs and the secure sanctuary: God made a secure sanctuary (haram amin) while people around are snatched away; Seafarers cry to God in a storm; what they do once rescued [contrast between the texts]; Was not God's earth wide enough for you to emigrate (hijra) in it?; Seafarers cry to God in a storm; what they do once rescued [divergence between the texts]; Sailors in a storm call on God sincerely, vow thanks, and transgress once saved; The life of this world is only amusement and play (lahw wa-la'ib); the abode of the hereafter is the true life; Every soul shall taste death; God provides prey for the lion and food for the raven's young that cry to him; If asked who created heaven and earth and sends rain, the idolaters themselves answer 'God'; Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

summary: These two units share 1 motifs: let them laugh a little and weep much.

Only in Better-than sayings (name, mourning, end of a thing): Do not be quick to anger, for anger lodges in the bosom of fools; Do not say 'Why were the former days better than these?', for it is not from wisdom you ask this; The end of a thing is better than its beginning; patience is better than pride; Like the crackling of thorns (sirim) under a pot (sir), so is the laughter of the fool; In the day of prosperity be joyful, in the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other; A good name is better than good oil (shem / shemen), and the day of death than the day of birth; Better to go to the house of mourning than to the house of feasting, for that is the end of all men; the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; Oppression makes a wise man foolish and a bribe destroys the heart; Vexation is better than laughter, for by sadness of face the heart is made glad; Consider the work of God: who can make straight what he has made crooked?; Wisdom is a shelter (shade) as money is a shelter; wisdom gives life to its possessor; A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, favor rather than silver and gold; and 1 more.

Only in Those who stayed behind, the exempt, and the Bedouin: The Bedouin (al-a'rab) are harder in unbelief and hypocrisy; Shirkers say 'do not go out in the heat'; hell's fire is hotter; Poor volunteers turn away weeping because the prophet has no mounts for them; Who is excused from going out to war [divergence between the texts]; Even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of joy is grief; The prophet must never pray over a dead hypocrite or stand at his grave; Catalogue of believers: repenting, worshiping, praising, wandering/fasting (sa'ihun), bowing, prostrating, enjoining right; God uses the unbelievers' wealth and children to punish them in this life; Hypocrites swear excuses and ask permission to stay behind from the campaign; Exemptions from war for a new house, unharvested vineyard, betrothed bride, or faintheartedness; God seals (tab') the hearts of deniers so they do not hear.

title: Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution ↔ The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: when the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, god is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back!.

passages.note: When the soul reaches the throat at death and you look on, God is nearer than you; if you are not to be judged, bring it back! (No man can hold back the departing spirit: ʾên ʾāḏām šallîṭ bā-rûaḥ li-ḵlôʾ ʾeṯ hā-rûaḥ wə-ʾên šilṭôn bə-yôm ham-māweṯ vs. fa-lawlā idhā balaghati l-ḥulqūm ... fa-lawlā in kuntum ghayra madīnīna tarjiʿūnahā in kuntum ṣādiqīn. Qohelet states it as a limit of human power; the Quran turns it into a challenge: if you are not to be judged, bring the soul back.)

Only in Obeying the king, the hour of death and the failure of retribution: Because sentence (pitgam) against an evil deed is not executed speedily, the heart of men is set to do evil; There are righteous men who receive what the wicked deserve and wicked who receive what the righteous deserve; No man has power over the wind (ruah) to restrain it, nor power over the day of death; there is no discharge in war; Keep the king's command because of the oath of God; who can say to him 'What are you doing?'; I saw the wicked buried with honor, going in and out of the holy place, and praised in the city where they did such things; Who is like the wise and knows the interpretation (pesher) of a thing? Wisdom makes his face shine; Man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun; even if the wise man claims to know, he cannot find it; For everything there is a season and a time for every matter under heaven (birth and death, planting and uprooting, etc.); Who will bring him to see what will be after him?; Wisdom or the fear of YHWH adds days and years of life; the years of the wicked are shortened; Human days on earth are a shadow; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

Only in The Companions of the Left in smoke and samum; who creates semen, crops, rain and fire?; the hidden Book; the soul at the throat: The damned eat of Zaqqum to fill their bellies and drink boiling water like thirst-crazed camels (al-him); A noble Quran in a hidden Book which none touch but the purified; The 'hospitality' (nuzul) of the deniers is boiling water and roasting in hell; The damned had lived in luxury and persisted in the great sin (al-hinth al-'azim); 'I swear by the positions (setting-places) of the stars, a mighty oath if you knew'; Have you seen the water you drink? Did you send it down from the rain-clouds? We could make it bitter (ujaj); For those brought near: rest (rawh), fragrance (rayhan) and a garden of bliss; The Companions of the Left are in scorching wind (samum), boiling water and the shade of black smoke (yahmum), neither cool nor kind; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Have you seen what you sow? Do you make it grow, or are we the grower? We could make it chaff; Fire kindled from a tree that God made grow [divergence between the texts]; The scripture exists with God in the 'Mother of the Book' (umm al-kitab), a heavenly archetype; and 8 more.

title: Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city ↔ Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only time (al-dahr) destroys us.

passages.note: Deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only Time (al-dahr) destroys us (Time as the impersonal power over men: kî ʿēṯ wā-p̄egaʿ yiqreh ʾeṯ kullām (time and chance befall them all) vs. wa-mā yuhlikunā illā d-dahr. Qohelet sets this beside faith in God; the Quran treats it as the deniers' creed.)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): echo. Time as the impersonal power over men: kî ʿēṯ wā-p̄egaʿ yiqreh ʾeṯ kullām (time and chance befall them all) vs. wa-mā yuhlikunā illā d-dahr. Qohelet sets this beside faith in God; the Quran treats it as the deniers' creed.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Deniers say there is only this life; we die and live, and only Time (al-dahr) destroys us (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Time and chance; the poor wise man who saved the city: Man does not know his time; like fish caught in a net and birds in a snare, people are trapped in an evil time; A great king besieges a small city; a poor wise man delivers it by his wisdom, yet no one remembers him; The race is not to the swift nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise; time and chance (pega') happen to all; Wisdom is better than might and weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good; A wise man scales the city of the mighty and brings down its trusted stronghold; 'Better is X than Y' comparative saying (tov ... min).

Only in Desire as god, 'only Time destroys us', and every nation kneeling before its book: God's book speaks against them with truth: 'We used to have transcribed (nastansikh) all that you did'; What God's heavenly book records: names or deeds [divergence between the texts]; Deniers of resurrection say there is only our first death and challenge the prophet to bring back their fathers; To God belongs the grandeur (kibriya') in the heavens and the earth; Whether death is the end: asked, held by sceptics, or answered by resurrection [response between the texts]; On the day of the Hour every community is seen kneeling (jathiya), each called to its book of deeds; Whoever takes his own desire (hawā) as his god; The prophet's mission and the hearers' closed ears, eyes and hearts: caused, sealed, or beyond his cure [divergence between the texts]; God forgets the damned today as they forgot the meeting of this day; Do evildoers think God will make them equal to the righteous in life and in death?; God did not create the heavens and earth and what is between them in play (la'ibin) but in truth; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; and 2 more.

title: Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal ↔ Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: the queen consults her chiefs, who defer to her; she observes that kings who enter a town ruin it and humble its nobles.

Only in Ahasuerus's banquets and Queen Vashti's refusal: Royal decree that every man shall rule in his own house; Merry with wine, the king orders the queen brought in her crown to show her beauty to his guests; A decree written into the laws of Persia and Media cannot be revoked; At the royal banquet drinking is by rule, no one compelled; The disobedient queen is deposed and her royalty given to 'another better than she'; The queen refuses to come at the king's command and the king is enraged; King holds a banquet showing his riches for 180 days; The queen holds a separate banquet for the women; Seven named eunuchs serve the king; Palace garden decorated with fine hangings, marble columns, gold and silver couches and mosaic pavement; Susa the citadel (Shushan ha-birah) as setting; Royal decree sent to each province in its own script and each people in its own language; and 2 more.

Only in Solomon, the speech of birds, the ants, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba: Entering Solomon's palace, the queen takes its floor of smooth glass for a pool and bares her legs; The hoopoe returns with sure news from Sabaʾ, knowledge Solomon lacked; Solomon sends the hoopoe to drop his letter before the queen and wait for their reply; Solomon reviews the birds, finds the hoopoe absent and threatens to punish or slaughter it unless it brings a clear excuse; An ʿifrīt of the jinn offers to bring the queen's throne before Solomon rises from his seat; Solomon's letter begins 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' and demands submission; The queen sends a gift to see what the envoys bring back; Solomon rejects the wealth and threatens invasion; The queen confesses she wronged herself and submits with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds; Solomon has the queen's throne disguised to test whether she recognizes it; she says 'It is as though it were it'; The queen and her people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Solomon inherits from David (knowledge and kingship); Solomon prays to be inspired to thank God for favor to him and his parents and to be admitted among the righteous; and 22 more.

Only in Israel multiplies; oppression; the Hebrew midwives; decree to drown sons: Midwives observe the newborn on the birthstool (ovnayim, 'the two stones'); Oppressed people forced to build store-cities with mortar and bricks; God rewards the God-fearing midwives by making them houses (families); Midwives excuse themselves: Hebrew women are vigorous and give birth before the midwife arrives; Two named midwives fear God and disobey the king's order to kill boys; A new king arises who did not know the former benefactor; The more the people are oppressed, the more they multiply; The people 'swarm' (sharats) and fill the land like creatures in creation; Ruler fears the immigrant people will grow numerous and join his enemies; How Egypt remembers Joseph [divergence between the texts]; Rulers fear that a people will leave the land, or drive them out of it [divergence between the texts]; The oppressor slaughters the sons and lets the women live; and 5 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; and 42 more.

title: The pursuit and the parting of the sea ↔ Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith
summary: These two units share 5 motifs: pharaoh acknowledges israel's god or his own sin, and what follows, why pharaoh pursues the departing israelites, what becomes of the drowned pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts], the king's heart is hardened (by himself or by god) so he refuses to release the people….

Exod gives it to the Egyptians as a group, Q to Pharaoh alone. cf. Pirqe de-R. Eliezer 43 and Mekhilta (Pharaoh survives and repents), outside the canon. Why Pharaoh pursues: in Exod regret at losing the slave labour (mah-zōʾt ʿāśînû kî-šillaḥnû ʾet-yiśrāʾēl mēʿobdēnû); in Q aggression and enmity (fa-atbaʿahum firʿawnu wa-junūduhu baghyan wa-ʿadwan). wa-jāwaznā bi-banī isrāʾīla l-baḥra fa-atbaʿahum firʿawnu ... ḥattā idhā adrakahu l-gharaq vs wayyāšūbû hammayim wayᵉkassû ʾet-hārekeb ... lᵉkōl ḥêl parʿōh. The drowned are seen as a sign afterwards: fa-l-yawma nunajjīka bi-badanika li-takūna li-man khalfaka āyatan vs wayyarʾ yiśrāʾēl ʾet-miṣrayim mēt ʿal-śᵉpat hayyām. Exod shows the Egyptian dead on the shore to Israel then; Q singles out Pharaoh's body, saved from the sea as a sign for later generations.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Pharaoh acknowledges Israel's God or his own sin, and what follows (weight 6.7); Why Pharaoh pursues the departing Israelites (weight 6.7); What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 29.2.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? The means differ: Exod has Moses stretch out his hand and YHWH drive the sea back by a strong east wind all night (bərûaḥ qādîm ʿazzâ kol-hallaylâ); Q has God tell Moses to strike a road, with the night departure (asri bi-ʿibādī) and 'fear not being overtaken'. wayyirdəpû miṣrayim ... wayyāšubû hammayim wayəkassû ʾet-hārekeb; fa-atbaʿahum Firʿawnu bi-junūdihi fa-ghashiyahum mina l-yammi mā ghashiyahum: the pursuing army is covered by the sea (ksh / ghšy, 'cover').

Shared motifs, rarest first: The people walk on dry ground through the sea with the waters as a wall on either side [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); King regrets releasing the slaves and pursues them with chariots (weight 6.3); The people walk on dry ground through the sea with the waters as a wall on either side (weight 5.3); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 22.8.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward'; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

Only in The night departure, the dry road through the sea, the mount and manna: The covenant appointment is at the right (ayman) side of the Mount (al-Ṭūr); A mountain called the mountain of God; Manna named from the people's question 'What is it?' (man hu); Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people.

title: The pursuit and the parting of the sea ↔ Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Motive for the pursuit: Exodus gives Pharaoh's regret (mah zōʾt ʿāśînû kî šillaḥnû ʾet Yiśrāʾēl mēʿovdēnû) and God hardening his heart so he will pursue and God be glorified (wə-ḥizzaqtî ʾet lēv Parʿōh wə-rādaf ʾaḥărêhem wə-ʾikkāvədâ bə-Farʿōh); Q 26:52 says only that God warned Moses 'innakum muttabaʿūn', and 26:54-55 gives Pharaoh's contempt (la-shirdhimatun qalīlūna ... la-ghāʾiẓūn). There is no regret over losing slaves and no hardening. fa-arsala Firʿawnu fī l-madāʾini ḥāshirīna ~ wa-yyeʾsōr ʾet rikbô wə-ʾet ʿammô lāqaḥ ʿimmô wa-yyiqqaḥ šēš mēʾôt rekhev bāḥûr: Pharaoh musters his force; Exodus counts chariots, the Quran sends heralds to the cities. qāla aṣḥābu Mūsā innā la-mudrakūna qāla kallā inna maʿiya rabbī sa-yahdīni ~ wə-hinnēh Miṣrayim nōsēaʿ ʾaḥărêhem wa-yyîrəʾû məʾōd ... ʾal tîrāʾû hityaṣṣəvû û-rəʾû ʾet yəšûʿat YHWH: the people see the pursuers and panic, and Moses calms them. In Exodus they complain bitterly (14:11-12); in the Quran they only state 'we are overtaken'. an iḍrib bi-ʿaṣāka l-baḥra fa-nfalaqa ~ hārēm ʾet maṭṭəkā û-nəṭēh ʾet yādəkā ʿal hay-yām û-vəqāʿēhû ... wa-yyôlekh YHWH ʾet hay-yām bə-rûaḥ qādîm ʿazzâ kol hal-laylâ: the split (infalaqa / vāqaʿ) follows the staff in both, but the Quran has Moses strike the sea, and it splits at once; the strong east wind blowing all night is gone. fa-nfalaqa ... wa-anjaynā Mūsā wa-man maʿahu ajmaʿīna ~ wa-yyāvōʾû vənê Yiśrāʾēl bə-tôkh hay-yām bay-yabbāšâ wə-ham-mayim lāhem ḥōmâ: passage through the divided sea; the Quran images the waters as mountains (ṭawd), Exodus as a wall (ḥōmâ). thumma aghraqnā l-ākharīna ~ wa-yyāšuvû ham-mayim wa-yəkhassû ʾet hā-rekhev ... lōʾ nišʾar bāhem ʿad ʾeḥād: the waters return over the pursuers and none survives.

Pair score 55.1.

Only in The pursuit and the parting of the sea: God's angel and the cloud pillar move behind the fleeing people to screen them from the pursuers; Israel camps by the sea opposite Baal-zephon, Migdol and Pi-hahiroth; God removes or clogs the wheels of the pursuers' chariots; The rescued people see the enemy dead on the seashore; At the morning watch God looks down from the pillar of fire and cloud and panics the enemy; God sets a trap so the enemy pursues and is destroyed, gaining glory over him; After the deliverance the people believe in God and in Moses his servant; The people say it would be better to serve their oppressors than die in the wilderness; God tells the praying leader: 'Why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward'; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; What becomes of the drowned Pharaoh and his army after the sea [divergence between the texts]; and 12 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; and 34 more.

passages.note: A mountain shaken by God's descent or by his revelation [divergence between the texts] (A mountain under the weight of revelation. Exodus: wə-har sînay ʿāšan kullô mip-pənê ʾăšer yāraḏ ʿālâw YHWH bā-ʾēš ... wa-yyeḥĕraḏ kol hā-hār məʾōḏ (Sinai actually smokes and quakes as YHWH descends). Exod: the mother's own plan, after hiding him three months, wattiqqaḥ-lô tēbat gōmeʾ wattaḥmərâ baḥēmār ûbazzāpet ... wattāśem bassûp ʿal-śəpat hayʾōr, set carefully among the reeds. Q: God reveals it to her (idh awḥaynā ilā ummika), iqdhifīhi fī t-tābūti fa-qdhifīhi fī l-yamm fa-l-yulqihi l-yammu bi-s-sāḥil: she throws the box into the river and the river casts it ashore by God's command. Exod: Pharaoh's daughter finds him, takes pity (wattaḥmōl ʿālāyw) and adopts and names him (wayhî-lāh ləbēn wattiqrāʾ šəmô mōšeh). Q: the finder is 'an enemy to me and an enemy to him' (yaʾkhudhhu ʿaduwwun lī wa-ʿaduwwun lah), and the love comes from God, wa-alqaytu ʿalayka maḥabbatan minnī. The naming and the rescuer's compassion are dropped. wattōʾmer ʾăḥōtô ʾel-bat-parʿōh hăʾēlēk wəqārāʾtî lāk ʾiššâ mêneqet min hāʿibriyyōt ... wattiqrāʾ ʾet-ʾēm hayyāled; idh tamshī ukhtuka fa-taqūlu hal adullukum ʿalā man yakfuluh fa-rajaʿnāka ilā ummika kay taqarra ʿaynuhā wa-lā taḥzan. Q gives the motive as the mother's comfort; Exod has the wages (ʾetten ʾet-śəkārēk). wayyak ʾet-hammiṣrî wayyiṭmənēhû baḥôl ... wayyîrāʾ mōšeh ... wayyibraḥ mōšeh mippənê parʿōh wayyēšeb bəʾereṣ-midyān; wa-qatalta nafsan fa-najjaynāka mina l-ghammi wa-fatannāka futūnan fa-labithta sinīna fī ahli Madyan. The killing and the flight to Midian are the same; Q retells them as God rescuing Moses from distress and testing him. Exod makes Moses' fear and Pharaoh's hunt the reason.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. At the water of Midian: Exodus has seven daughters of the priest of Midian (šebaʿ bānôt) who draw water, shepherds who drive them off (wa-ygārəšûm), and Moses who rescues them (wa-yyôšiʿān) and waters their flock. The Quran has two women holding back their flock (imraʾatayni tadhūdāni) until the shepherds finish, explaining abūnā shaykhun kabīrun; Moses waters for them unasked, then withdraws to the shade and prays (rabbi innī limā anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqīr). There is no fight with the shepherds. The father: Exodus has a named priest, kōhēn Midyān and Rəʿûʾēl, who scolds his daughters for leaving the stranger and invites him to eat (qirʾen lô wə-yōʾkhal leḥem); the Quran has an unnamed 'very old man' (shaykhun kabīr), no priest, who sends a daughter to pay Moses his wage (li-yajziyaka ajra mā saqayta lanā) and reassures him: lā takhaf najawta mina l-qawmi ẓ-ẓālimīn. The daughters' role: in Exodus they report together to their father, ʾîš Miṣrî hiṣṣîlānû mi-yyad hā-rōʿîm, 'an Egyptian man saved us' (Moses taken for an Egyptian); in the Quran one daughter walks shyly (tamshī ʿalā stiḥyāʾ) to invite him and then advises her father, istaʾjirhu inna khayra mani staʾjarta l-qawiyyu l-amīnu, 'hire him, the best one to hire is the strong and trustworthy'. The marriage: Exodus has wa-yyôʾel Mōše lāševet ʾet hā-ʾîš wa-yyittēn ʾet Ṣippōrâ vittô lə-Mōše, a named bride and no terms; the Quran has an unnamed daughter given under a contract of service, ʿalā an taʾjuranī thamāniya ḥijajin fa-in atmamta ʿashran fa-min ʿindika, eight years or ten if he wishes, sworn before God (wa-llāhu ʿalā mā naqūlu wakīl).

summary: These two units share 7 motifs: how moses killed the egyptian [divergence between the texts], how moses learns that his life is sought [divergence between the texts], kinsman rebuffs the hero: 'who made you prince and judge over us?', hero kills an oppressor beating a kinsman and hides the body in the sand….

passages.note: How Moses killed the Egyptian [divergence between the texts] (The killing: Exodus has Moses see an Egyptian beating a Hebrew 'of his brothers', look this way and that and see no one (wa-yyifen kōh wā-khōh wa-yyarʾ kî ʾên ʾîš), strike him and hide him in the sand. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. The killing: Exodus has Moses see an Egyptian beating a Hebrew 'of his brothers', look this way and that and see no one (wa-yyifen kōh wā-khōh wa-yyarʾ kî ʾên ʾîš), strike him and hide him in the sand. The Quran has him find two men fighting, one of his party (shīʿa) and one of his enemy; at his kinsman's cry for help he strikes one blow and the man dies (fa-wakazahu Mūsā fa-qaḍā ʿalayhi). There is no looking around and no hiding of the body; the act is unpremeditated. Moral verdict on the killing: Exodus passes none; Moses only fears exposure (wa-yyîrāʾ Mōše wa-yyōʾmar ʾākhēn nôdaʿ had-dāvār). The Quran has Moses judge it at once, hādhā min ʿamali sh-shayṭān ... rabbi innī ẓalamtu nafsī fa-ghfir lī, and God forgives him (fa-ghafara lahu), so Moses is a repentant penitent before he is a prophet. The second day: in Exodus two Hebrews (šənê ʾănāšîm ʿIvrîm) fight, Moses rebukes the guilty one, and that Hebrew retorts mî śāməkhā lə-ʾîš śar wə-šōfēṭ ʿālênû ha-lə-hārəgēnî ʾattâ ʾōmēr ka-ʾăšer hāragtā ʾet ham-Miṣrî. In the Quran the same kinsman again calls for help against an enemy, Moses calls the kinsman 'clearly misguided' (la-ghawiyyun mubīn), and as he moves to strike the enemy he hears a-turīdu an taqtulanī kamā qatalta nafsan bi-l-amsi in turīdu illā an takūna jabbāran fī l-arḍ. 'Prince and judge' becomes 'tyrant' (jabbār). How the danger reaches Moses: Exodus has wa-yyišmaʿ Parʿōh ʾet had-dāvār haz-zeh wa-yvaqqēš lahărōg ʾet Mōše, Pharaoh himself; the Quran has the chiefs plotting (al-malaʾa yaʾtamirūna bika li-yaqtulūka) and an unnamed sympathizer running from the far end of the city to warn him (wa-jāʾa rajulun min aqṣā l-madīnati yasʿā). fa-kharaja minhā khāʾifan yataraqqabu ... wa-lammā tawajjaha tilqāʾa Madyana ~ wa-yyivraḥ Mōše mip-pənê Farʿōh wa-yyēšev bə-ʾereṣ Midyān: flight to Midian (Madyan / Midyān). The Quran adds two prayers (rabbi najjinī ... ʿasā rabbī an yahdiyanī sawāʾa s-sabīl).

Shared motifs, rarest first: How Moses killed the Egyptian [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); How Moses learns that his life is sought [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Kinsman rebuffs the hero: 'Who made you prince and judge over us?' (weight 6.7); Hero kills an oppressor beating a kinsman and hides the body in the sand (weight 6.7); The retort Moses hears on the day after the killing [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); How Moses' killing of the Egyptian is judged [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Hero flees the king's death sentence to a foreign land (weight 5.8). Pair score 45.5.

Only in Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry: The foundling's weeping moves the finder to compassion; The hero's parents are introduced anonymously as a Levite man and a Levite woman; Mother sees that her newborn 'is good' (ki tov); Hero names his son for being a stranger in a foreign land; Infant adopted by a royal woman [divergence between the texts]; The groaning of the oppressed rises to God, who hears and remembers his covenant; Hero drives off shepherds and waters the flock of women at a well; What the Midianite daughters do after Moses helps them [divergence between the texts]; Moses helps the women at the water of Midian [divergence between the texts]; Moses' father-in-law in Midian [divergence between the texts]; Moses killed a man and God delivered him from distress, then tried him with trials [divergence between the texts]; Who decides that Moses be put on the water [divergence between the texts]; and 19 more.

Only in Moses kills the Egyptian, is warned, and flees toward Midian: Moses calls his killing 'the work of Satan' and asks forgiveness, which is granted; A man comes running from the far end of the city to warn the hero that the chiefs plot to kill him; When Moses reached his full strength God gave him judgment and knowledge; Moses killed a man and God delivered him from distress, then tried him with trials.
